rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly with no ICE, so the table is pushed toward stronger obfuscation while respecting that this target is a bundle of tight numeric benchmark loops (nsieve bit-sieving, fannkuch, spectral-norm, n-body) where per-iteration overhead multiplies: BCF keeps the lowest cost-tolerance weights since bogus control flow is the worst runtime/size offender in hot loops, and FLA stays moderate for the same reason. SUB is given generous cost headroom because instruction substitution is nearly free and composes well with the arithmetic-heavy code, and IGV gets high DiversityGain since a single large main dominated by global state benefits strongly from variable-encoding diversity. IBR and ICALL receive solid SecurityGain/DiversityGain with restrained cost tolerance — indirect branches and calls are effective against static disassembly but add per-execution cost and slight correctness risk in a program with only two functions, so they are enabled but not maximally weighted. SPLIT stays enabled with low risk and high cost tolerance since splitting the 483-byte main is cheap and improves the effectiveness of every other pass. All seven passes remain considered because round 0 showed no correctness or build problems to avoid.
